result.topic_en: Euler models the friction on a fluid element in a tube as a small multiple λ of the pressure on the tube wall. He derives the resulting retardation λpu/zz and evaluates it for rectangular, square and circular cross-sections.

10. Pendet ergo frictio tam a quantitate, quam
a figura cauitatis tubi: si enim ponamus sectionem tubi
in MN factam, esse rectangularem, altero latere exi-

et area $zz=mn$, vnde hoc casu erit retardatio

retardatio $=\frac{4\lambda p}{n}$. Sin autem sectio sit circularis, dia-
metrum habens $=n$, ob $u=2\pi n$ et $zz=\pi nn$, erit
retardatio $=\frac{2\lambda p}{n}$.

items.english: Let the force of friction be denoted by λpuds, since friction bears a given ratio to the force of pressure puds.

items.quote: $\lambda$ esse fractionem valde paruam, cuius valor per experimenta determinari debet
items.english: λ is a very small fraction, whose value must be determined by experiments.

items.quote: erit ipsa retardatio a frictione oriunda $=\frac{\lambda pu}{zz}$
items.english: The retardation arising from friction will be λpu/zz.

items.quote: Pendet ergo frictio tam a quantitate, quam a figura cauitatis tubi
items.english: Therefore friction depends both on the size and on the shape of the tube's cavity.

items.quote: Sin autem sectio sit circularis, diametrum habens $=n$, ob $u=2\pi n$ et $zz=\pi nn$, erit retardatio $=\frac{2\lambda p}{n}$
items.english: If the section is circular with diameter n, then since u=2πn and zz=πnn, the retardation will be 2λp/n.
